code.displayName: History of Present illness Narrative

text.paragraph: Ms. O'Connor returns nine days after presenting with three months of painful, swollen hands, wrists, and knees, evening fevers, fatigue, a facial rash after sun, and protein and blood in her urine. She saw Dr. Okonjo-Strand this morning, and the tests drawn there returned this afternoon: ANA positive at 1:640 in a homogeneous pattern, anti-dsDNA 186 IU/mL, anti-Sm 42 U/mL, and low complements (C3 62, C4 8 mg/dL). Anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies are negative and the lupus anticoagulant test is negative. The urine protein-to-creatinine ratio is 1.8 g/g, with 22 red cells per high-power field, many of them misshapen, and a red cell cast; creatinine is 0.8. Hepatitis B surface antigen is negative with a positive surface antibody, and hepatitis C and HIV tests are negative; a pregnancy test is negative. Before the results were given she was asked how she wanted to hear them and said she wanted all of it, at once. She was told directly that she has systemic lupus erythematosus, that the urine findings mean the kidneys are probably involved, and that a kidney biopsy is needed to choose treatment; she knows that her father had lupus, and was told plainly that treatment and outlook today are very different. She repeated it back accurately. She asked that her diagnosis not be shared with anyone she has not named. [S]

code.displayName: Evaluation + Plan note

list.item:
Systemic lupus erythematosus (M32.19). The positive ANA meets the entry criterion, and the EULAR/ACR weighted classification criteria add up to 32 (fever 2, thrombocytopenia 4, acute cutaneous lupus 6, joint involvement 6, proteinuria above 0.5 g a day 4, low C3 and C4 4, anti-dsDNA or anti-Sm 6), well above the threshold of 10. The disease is highly active (SLEDAI-2K 23). Antiphospholipid antibodies are negative, which matters for contraception and any future pregnancy. This is lupus, not rheumatoid arthritis. [S]
Hydroxychloroquine 300 mg daily now (5 mg/kg), long term.
Sun protection every day.
No NSAIDs with kidney involvement; acetaminophen for pain.
Pneumococcal PCV20 and recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1 today, before immunosuppression.

Proteinuria with an active urine sediment (R80.9). Protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g with dysmorphic red cells and a red cell cast: lupus nephritis is likely, and the class determines treatment. Blood pressure 136/84 is above the target of 130/80. [S]
Ultrasound-guided kidney biopsy in two days.
Losartan 25 mg daily for proteinuria and blood pressure; potassium and creatinine in two to four weeks.

Contraception before immunosuppression. Mycophenolate, the likely treatment, causes birth defects and needs highly effective contraception. With negative antiphospholipid antibodies estrogen-containing methods are not ruled out, but with active disease she chose a levonorgestrel intrauterine system. [S]
Intrauterine system inserted before treatment starts.

list.item: Establish the diagnosis within two weeks and hear it directly, in plain words. Outcome by 1950-04-22: Told directly at nine days that she has systemic lupus erythematosus, with the reasons and a written summary [S]
Renal response: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio halved by three months and below 0.5 g/g with stable kidney function by six to twelve months. In progress; target 1950-10-26 [S]
Prednisone 5 mg a day or less by six months, with withdrawal considered later. In progress; target 1950-10-26 [S]
Write at least four mornings a week through treatment. In progress; target 1950-12-31 [S]
No unplanned pregnancy on mycophenolate; plan any pregnancy for a time of quiet disease on compatible medicines. In progress; target 1950-12-31 [S]
